name: Lark
tagline: One suite for chat, docs, and video that still waits for you to run it
painPoints: Value depends on full team adoption: if only part of the team uses Lark, the cross-product linking breaks down
Automations need manual rule setup and ongoing maintenance: nothing acts until you define triggers
No Gmail inbox management: external email stays outside Lark messenger
ByteDance ownership raises data residency questions for regulated teams
Consolidation means migration: chat, docs, calendar, and video must all move to Lark to get the benefit
metaTitle: Best Lark Alternative: Open-Source AI Assistant
metaDescription: Looking for a Lark alternative? GAIA is open-source AI that triages email, manages tasks, and runs workflows across 50+ tools. Free tier included.
whyPeopleLook: Lark promises one suite for chat, docs, calendar, and video. It works when the whole team moves. Most teams do not move. They keep Gmail, Slack, GitHub, and Notion, and Lark becomes one more platform to check. People looking for a Lark alternative want AI that works across the tools they already use, without a migration and without manual rule setup.
gaiaReplaces: Meeting prep from calendar and inbox context
Task creation from email without rule setup
Follow-ups that span Gmail, Slack, and docs
Workflow automation described in plain English
gaiaAdvantages: Works across your existing tools with no suite migration required
Acts proactively on email and calendar without manual trigger configuration
Open source and self-hostable for full data control
Free tier available; self-hosting is free with no per-seat cost
migrationSteps: Keep Lark for team chat and video while you evaluate
Connect Gmail and Google Calendar to GAIA for inbox and schedule context
Delegate one recurring workflow to GAIA, such as meeting prep or email triage
Expand to Slack, Notion, or your task tool once the first workflow sticks

faqs.question: Can GAIA replace Lark chat, docs, and video?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA does not provide team chat, video meetings, or co-editing docs. It connects to tools you already use, such as Gmail, Slack, and Google Calendar, and automates work across them. Teams that need an all-in-one suite still need dedicated chat and video alongside GAIA.

faqs.question: How does GAIA automation compare to Lark workflow rules?
faqs.answer: Lark runs automations you configure with triggers and conditions inside its platform. GAIA takes plain English instructions and orchestrates actions across connected tools. GAIA also monitors inbox and calendar context and surfaces next steps without a predefined trigger.

faqs.question: Is GAIA a good Lark alternative for privacy sensitive teams?
faqs.answer: GAIA is open source and self-hostable, so data stays on your own infrastructure. Lark is owned by ByteDance, which raises data residency questions for some regulated teams. Self-hosted GAIA gives you full control over where data lives.

faqs.question: How much does GAIA cost compared to Lark?
faqs.answer: GAIA offers a free tier and Pro from ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month, with self-hosting free and no per-seat charge. Lark paid plans scale per user, so GAIA is typically cheaper for small teams that want AI automation without migrating the whole suite.

comparisonRows.competitor: Lark AI assists with writing, summarizing docs, and generating content within the platform; workflow automation requires explicit rule configuration

comparisonRows.gaia: Full Gmail management: reads, triages, drafts replies, and creates tasks or notes from emails automatically
comparisonRows.competitor: No inbox management for external email; internal messaging handled through Lark's own messenger

comparisonRows.gaia: AI-powered task management with priorities, deadlines, and tasks auto-created from emails and conversations
comparisonRows.competitor: Built-in task management within Lark's project module; tasks linked to docs and messages within the platform

comparisonRows.gaia: Full Google Calendar integration: reads, creates, and updates events; generates pre-meeting briefings automatically
comparisonRows.competitor: Built-in calendar with meeting scheduling, availability sharing, and video meeting integration within Lark

comparisonRows.gaia: Continuously monitors email, calendar, and connected tools to surface insights and act before you ask
comparisonRows.competitor: Reactive platform: automations run on triggers you configure; no ambient monitoring of external workflow context

comparisonRows.gaia: 50+ integrations including Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, Todoist, Linear, Jira, and more via MCP
comparisonRows.competitor: 250+ app integrations within the Lark ecosystem; strong within its own suite but external integrations require configuration

comparisonRows.gaia: Natural language multi-step workflows with triggers and conditions spanning any connected tool: described in plain English
